germinated_from.note: THIS BODY WAS ADVERTISED BEFORE IT EXISTED. The collapse spore declared this stolon and could not finish the question: it could show contraction and not who profits from it. what: The archive's political economy of meaning, seeded at the stolon the collapse body left open. Its roles are NOT the collapse roles: where that body asks what narrows, this one asks who gains by the narrowing.
vocabulary_source:
REBUILT FROM THE DEFINING PAPERS, 2026-09-12. v0.1 scoped this body to the ten numbered extraction operators of #27 Operative Architecture. Those are ONE REGION — §3.2, the extraction problem — of a framework that has three (§3.1 labor, §3.2 extraction, §3.3 enclosure) and six economic forms. The scoping was done by pattern-matching vocabulary rather than by reading what the framework says it covers.

#623 SEMANTIC INFRASTRUCTURE: FROM TIM BERNERS-LEE TO THE SEMANTIC ECONOMY is the bridge paper and its §4 IS the filter — a mapping from technical operations to economic forms: ontology engineering as semantic LABOR, knowledge graphs as semantic CAPITAL, standards as semantic INFRASTRUCTURE, knowledge-panel and API use as semantic RENT, model ingestion as semantic LIQUIDATION, maintenance failure and recursive degradation as semantic EXHAUSTION.

#255 SEMANTIC LIQUIDATION: AN EXECUTIVE SUMMARY supplies the operation's internal structure — three properties (irreversibility, value transfer, invisibility) and five stages (tokenization, stripping, attribution relocation, value capture, closure).

#24 MIND-CONTROL POEMS supplies the counter-operation: alienation extended into the symbolic infrastructure through which labor, recognition and desire become thinkable, and the liberatory poem as a symbolic counter-operation that interrupts conditioning and restores contact with relation and historical possibility.

select.note: Built from the defining papers' own articulations rather than from vocabulary frequency. The six economic forms are #623 §4; the accounting questions are §7; the five stages are #255; the counter-operation is #24. A term is here because a founding paper uses it to do theoretical work, not because it recurs.

roles.note: #623 §4.1 — ontology engineering as semantic labor. Who does the work the value is taken from.
#623 §4.2 — knowledge graphs as semantic capital. Accumulated structured meaning, owned.
#623 §4.3 — standards as infrastructure. What everyone builds on and nobody is paid for.
#623 §4.4 — knowledge-panel and API use as rent. Charging for access to what was given.
#623 §4.4 and #255 — conversion of situated meaning into retrievable units, destroying context or authorship. Five stages, three properties.
#623 §4.5 — maintenance failure and recursive degradation. 'Model collapse is not a metaphor.'
#24 — the symbolic counter-operation. Not compensation alone; commons repair.

roles_note: ORDER IS THE CLASSIFIER and the order here is the mapping's own: labor, capital, infrastructure, rent, liquidation, exhaustion — the sequence #623 §4 uses, which runs from what is produced to what is destroyed. counter_operation and accounting follow because they act on the six rather than being among them.
stolons: THE RETURN EDGE. The collapse body advertised this one; this one advertises it back. What contraction looks like from the side of the ledger — the question the parent could not finish is answered here only in part, and the part it cannot finish is what contraction does to meaning itself.
erasure as a cost borne by the provenance-bearer and never by the composer — the asymmetry is the operation's economic form
the captures are where the economy is observable; 425 of them are not reproduced here

special_roles_note: A capture carrying a PER is the ACCOUNTING — an instrument's output. A capture without one is an INSTANCE: evidence the operation ran, with no claim about which of the six forms it took. Calling an unmeasured capture `liquidation` would assert the operation from the fact of a record, which is the thing this framework's own instruments exist to avoid asserting.
follow_note: THE FRONTIER EXPLODED AT 1,613 NEIGHBOURS on the first emission because the follow set included defines_concept, about and part_of_line — predicates that fan out across the whole archive. A frontier is one typed hop from a body, not one hop from a category. The collapse grammar keeps them because its core is concept-anchored; this body's core is deposit-anchored and cannot afford them.
extent_test: §7: 'What remains incomplete is the governance of that infrastructure — THE ACCOUNTING OF WHO PRODUCES, WHO EXTRACTS, AND WHO BENEFITS.' A deposit is in this body's extent if it bears on that accounting in the economy of meaning-production. §6 states why this is not a metaphor and the reason matters for the filter: 'the framework does not impose economic categories on non-economic phenomena — it reveals the economic dynamics that were always present but lacked vocabulary.' So model collapse is inside as semantic EXHAUSTION ('model collapse is not a metaphor'), knowledge panels are inside as semantic RENT, and the capture registry is inside as the measurement of extraction. They are not adjacent bodies; they are regions the mapping already names.
kinds_note:
A SECOND AXIS, ORTHOGONAL TO FORM. The roles say what economic form a deposit NAMES — labor, capital, infrastructure, rent, liquidation, exhaustion. They do not say what KIND OF WORK it does. PER names liquidation and IS an instrument; #623 names all six and IS theory. Crossing the two separates a body that argues from one that measures, which the form axis alone cannot do.

THE SOURCE IS THE ARCHIVE'S OWN content_type FIELD, not a new judgment — but it is free text with 37 distinct values across 89 deposits, one of them a sixty-word paragraph, so it is normalised here by an ordered mapping and the unmapped fall to `unkinded` rather than being forced.

#137 §10.0 and §11 license the instrument/theory split in this framework's own terms: 'Efficacy Before Falsifiability — the instrument must bite', and 'the instrument is not a coinage — it is one operator in a standing system'. An instrument is a distinct kind with its own obligations.
kinds: a thing that measures or acts, not a thing that argues. #137 §10.0: the instrument must bite.

organized.reading:
THE THIN COLUMNS ARE THE FINDING. 7 instruments and 3 practices against 48 measurements: the body measures far more than it has instruments to measure with, which is consistent with PER doing most of the work alone and with #137 §11's claim that the instrument 'is one operator in a standing system' — a system with seven members.

SEMANTIC_RENT HAS NO INSTRUMENT AND NO MEASUREMENT. Knowledge-panel and API use is the mechanism by which value is captured — #623 §4.4 — and this body can argue about it and cannot measure it. That is the largest single gap the grid exposes and it is directly commercial: rent is where the money is, and it is the one form with no meter.

SEMANTIC_INFRASTRUCTURE IS BUILT RATHER THAN ARGUED — 11 specifications against 6 theory, the most built-out region. SEMANTIC_LIQUIDATION IS THE REVERSE: 5 works against 1 theory, the operation written through more than written about. accounting is 34 measurements and nothing else, which is correct — it is an instrument's output, not an argument.
organized.caution: The kind axis is normalised from a free-text field by an ordered regex mapping. It covers every deposit in this body and zero fall to `unkinded`, but coverage is not accuracy: a deposit whose content_type says 'Theoretical paper' is filed as theory on the strength of its own label.
